The man studied Kiran's birth date and said, "You are independent, but you secretly want people's approval." Kiran grinned. "Would the opposite also fit? Wanting approval, but secretly independent?" He laughed and agreed it might. "Then tell me something I could check," Kiran said. "Which month will my team lead reply about the Bengaluru transfer?" The transfer would be decided on the pay and on being near family, not on energies.

Losar night, Darjeeling. Writing this by the heater.
Binita's aunt reads tea leaves every year, and tonight she held my cup up to the lamp. 'Tenzin, you work very hard but sometimes doubt yourself. A big decision is coming over water.' Everyone went 'ooh' because they all know about the Singapore offer.
I liked it, honestly. It felt warm. But I asked, 'Aunty, would "you're confident but sometimes lazy" fit me too?' She laughed and said, 'Also true!' Binita kicked me under the table.
Then I asked if the leaves could say anything I could check, like the salary or when they'll reply. 'Leaves don't do numbers,' she said. Fair.
So, notes to self: I do doubt myself. Worth thinking about. But the offer gets decided on the contract, the team and whether I want to be that far from Amala. Not a teacup.
Still, the butter tea was excellent.

qa.a: She said, 'A big decision is coming over water.'

qa.a: Tenzin liked it and found it warm, and took the line about self-doubt as worth thinking about, while not treating it as a prediction.
